To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) homelessness in Wallonia is a complex phenomenon that cannot be understood by looking at a single cause; (ii) the geography of homelessness in Wallonia has to be understood in a broader perspective, including both urban slums and rural holiday parks; (iii) the geography of pathways to homelessness is not linear, but rather a complex and multi-layered network of pathways; (iv) there is an urgent need to develop collective policies to fight against homelessness.
the geography of pathways of the households who live in the holiday parks in Wallonia is characterized by a rural background, an urban background, or a rural-urban background.

(1) the majority of homeless households living in holiday parks are not originally from the rural areas where these parks are located, (2) most households have been in a state of homelessness for a long time, and (3) the majority of households have a history of urban slum living.

holiday parks are not a solution for the problem of homelessness, but a problem in itself, as they are a temporary solution for a structural problem.
